$comment: THE REPLACEMENT LIFECYCLE (docs/city/OWNER_CONTINUOUS_CONSTRUCTION_WORKBOOK.md section 21, principle 15.4). Section 21 requires a REUSABLE mechanism, not a one-off migration, and says plainly: 'Do not attempt to replace every capability merely to exercise this.' So this artifact is the PROTOCOL -- a state machine plus the seven pieces of machinery section 21 enumerates -- and instances are declared against it. The reason it is machine-checked rather than documented is the failure mode: a replacement that reports RETIRED without ever having run both sides side by side is indistinguishable, in prose, from one that did. The validator refuses a history that SKIPS a state, so the lifecycle cannot be claimed without being walked.
adoptionProtocol: A capability that wants to be replaced declares an instance here with the seven pieces of machinery section 21 names, then walks the history one state at a time, recording for each state the evidence the machine asks for and the ledger entry that records the step. No new protocol is needed: the states, the transitions and the evidence requirements are in this artifact, and the validator is generic over instances -- a case in tests/unit/city/replacement-lifecycle.test.ts drives a SECOND synthetic instance for a different capability through the same validator to prove that no capability-specific logic is hiding in it.

P2A-BRIDGE-01-RETIREMENT.whatIsReplaced: an import PATH, not a capability: the one-symbol re-export of ProviderId added by the P2-A provider closure (ledger CC-029) so that five tests/acceptance/** suites could keep importing from ./contracts while the type moved to src/shared/provider-contracts.ts. The retained unit is a symbol's import path; a capability-level instance remains for a future migration, and section 21's acceptance is met by this one only in the 'one real, bounded migration' sense, which the record states explicitly rather than implying more.
P2A-BRIDGE-01-RETIREMENT.authoritativeSide: src/shared/contracts.ts, owned by `status`: the statement `export type { ProviderId } from "./provider-contracts";`
P2A-BRIDGE-01-RETIREMENT.successorSide: src/shared/provider-contracts.ts, owned by `providers`: the ProviderId declaration itself
P2A-BRIDGE-01-RETIREMENT.shadowMode: the successor is ALREADY serving every consumer that imports it directly, while the old side serves only the five tests/acceptance/** suites that still import from ./contracts -- so both sides are live at once and the comparison is available before any switch
P2A-BRIDGE-01-RETIREMENT.dualOutputComparison: typecheck IS the comparison: both paths must resolve ProviderId to the same declaration. `npx tsc --noEmit` over tsconfig.json, tsconfig.electron.json and tsconfig.tests.json, plus tests/unit/city/provider-closure.test.ts, prove the two sides are the same type rather than two types that merely look alike.
P2A-BRIDGE-01-RETIREMENT.trafficSwitch: change the five imports in tests/acceptance/** from ./contracts to ./provider-contracts, in one commit, and delete the re-export in the same commit
P2A-BRIDGE-01-RETIREMENT.rollback: restore the re-export line in src/shared/contracts.ts and revert the five import edits; the successor file is never modified by this migration, so a rollback cannot lose work and cannot leave a half-moved surface
P2A-BRIDGE-01-RETIREMENT.drain: the measurement that no consumer remains: a scan of tests/acceptance/** for a ProviderId import from ./contracts must return zero, which is the check that turns 'I moved them' into a number
